FILED s543 by the reviewing session (2026-11-22, evening), found by the review probes of s543h's brace-name change (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1122/rh3 c-07 .. c-09).  PRE-EXISTING: main b58114ca (MAIN-READY-106), s543h's tree 9b024238 and s543i's tree all the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40 | ./runpcl on main):
    "abc" =~ /(b)(c)/; my $x = ${1}; my @l = (${1}, ${2});
    print "G: $x @l [${1}] ", ${1} . "!", "\n";        # G: b b c [b] b!   |  G: 1 1 2 [b] 1!
    print "H: <$0> <${0}> <", ${0}, ">\n";             # <d1.pl> <d1.pl> <d1.pl>  |  <d1.pl> <d1.pl> <0>
    print eval('${1} . ${2}'), "\n";                   # bc  |  12

WHAT IT IS: in code the brace spelling of an all-digit name (`${1}`, `${0}`, `${12}`) yields the digits themselves; the interpolating spelling `"${1}"` is right (InterpScan knows it).  `${_}` and `${;}` are right.  PPI gives a Cast + a Block holding a Number; the block's VALUE is taken where perl takes the NAME (perl: `${ DIGITS }` and `${ IDENTIFIER }` are the variable, never a block).

FIX DIRECTION: the brace-NAME reading has ONE helper since s543h -- Parser2::_brace_name_refs (a Word in a Cast's Block) -- used by the rewriter and, since 9b024238, by the requalifier's candidate list.  A Number that is all digits in a Cast's Block is the same spelling: teach THAT helper (and whatever lowers the Word case to a variable read) rather than a second reader.  Check `@{1}`-style and `$#{1}` only as far as perl accepts them; `${1}[0]` / `${1}{k}` are elements of @1 / %1 (cf. #1679, s543i).  BAR: the reproducer rows + the eval row + a write (`${1}` is read-only in perl: the write dies there too -- probe it).


=== DONE (s543k) === (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22/23; WIP 6)
PExpr::_collapse_braced_bareword_derefs (the lowering of the Word case) takes PExpr::_block_sole_digits (a block holding exactly one all-digit Number) and builds the token PPI makes for the PLAIN spelling ($N / @N Magic, %N Symbol, $#N ArrayIndex) -- a subscript after it is the element of @N / %N (#1679's lowering); Parser2::_brace_name_refs reads the same predicate and the binder records the brace ref.  `${ +1 }`, `${ \ 1 }`, `${ 1; }` stay blocks.
